A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CARL and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Their shared content can be matched reliably despite substantial revisions and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original retina experiments and CARL medical-registration results in Section 6, plus an original IXI evaluation in Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 reports original medical-registration results, rotation experiments, refinement ablations, and feature and attention analyses.

M1.justification: V3 adds a third refinement layer to CARL in Eq. 16. It also introduces CARL{ROT}, using rotated encoder averaging, an additional dilation-8 convolution, rotation augmentation with modified loss composition, and revised displacement-field extrapolation. These change the architecture and computational procedure.

E1.justification: V3 adds rotated-HCP evaluation scenarios and SO(3) rotation-augmented training, extending beyond v1's translation tests. Conversely, v1's separate IXI brain-registration experiment in Appendix D is removed. The retina, COPDGene/DirLab, HCP, Abdomen1k, and Learn2Reg coverage remains.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds uniGradICON with and without instance optimization to the Abdomen1k comparison. Learn2Reg validation gains ConvexAdam, supervised and unsupervised Estienne entries, and uniGradICON without instance optimization. The separate IXI comparison against published KeyMorph weights and ANTs disappears, while most existing comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: Reported CARL training with GradICON regularization increases from 50,000 to 100,000 steps, with the final refinement layer introduced after 50,000 steps. New protocols include rotation augmentation and evaluation, direct transformation-discrepancy measurements, two-image linear probing, and inspection of 25 randomly selected attention queries. Existing dataset splits and the 30 Abdomen1k test pairs are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds a final-refinement ablation (Table 2), rotation robustness tests (Figure 4), feature probes and attention-compactness checks (Figures 9–10), direct equivariance-error measurements (Figure 11), and additional registration case studies (Figures 12–14). The earlier retina ablations, organ-level analyses, and two-step loss-landscape analysis remain.

E5.justification: V1's checklist explicitly discloses only 1–2 training runs per medical dataset; v3 omits this information. Synthetic-run distributions and organ-level boxplots remain. The PDFs do not establish an increase in repeated runs or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes CARL's Abdomen1k Dice from 74.1 to 75.7, HCP Dice from 78.8 to 79.6, DirLab mTRE from 2.58 to 1.88, and Learn2Reg validation CARL(IO) Dice from 53 to 56. These accompany architecture and training-budget changes, rather than establishing same-setting gains. Several earlier scores remain in v3's refinement ablation. Rotation results and baseline entries are added, Figure 4 revises GradICON translation curves, and the IXI results disappear.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix C.2 assumes inverse consistency and contains an incomplete exact-recovery derivation. V3 Section 10.2 instead requires identity output for identical images and repairs the derivation. V3 also supplies explicit interpolation steps and an affine-attention lemma proof in Section 18, plus new rotation-training and extrapolation derivations in Sections 15–16.

C1.justification: V3 expands the contribution from translation-equivariant registration to include rotation equivariance learned through augmentation. Its abstract also broadens the performance claim from outperforming unsupervised abdomen-registration approaches to matching or outperforming state-of-the-art methods across all evaluated datasets.

C2.justification: The earlier unsuccessful rotation-extension discussion is replaced by an explanation of CARL{ROT}, including its boundary-effect tradeoff with translation equivariance. V3 distinguishes learned identity-output behavior from architectural guarantees and tentatively links poor pancreas registration to missing pancreas information in linear probes. V1's societal-impact discussion is removed.

D1.justification: V3 provides implementation instructions for encoder averaging, added dilation, rotation-loss handling, and boundary extrapolation. It updates training-time and hardware information, including an A100 configuration. V1's code, experiment-log, and planned-license disclosures disappear with the checklist. A remaining reproducibility issue is that Section 6.3 and Appendix 15 use different inverse conventions for undoing rotation augmentation.

R1.justification: V3 adds MultiGradICON and expands the GradICON-family context. SynthSeg and brain-extraction references disappear with the IXI experiment, and the bias-related citation disappears with societal impacts. It also removes the assertion that loss-enforced equivariance is unlikely to generalize out of distribution. The main related-work organization and positioning remain.

P1.justification: Most main-text exposition and section order remain recognizable. V3 clarifies notation, renames Section 3, edits explanations and captions, updates affiliations, renumbers supplementary sections, and removes the submission checklist. The retained scientific narrative is largely preserved.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column layout to predominantly two columns. Figure 1 gains a rotated-brain example, Figure 4 expands to translation and rotation plots, and Table 1 gains rows and an unsupervised-status column. Supplementary figures are enlarged or rearranged, new Figures 9–14 appear, and the IXI table is replaced by a distinct refinement-ablation table.

improvement.justification: The repaired recovery guarantee and new attention, equivariance, refinement, and rotation analyses strengthen the paper's scientific support. The net improvement is limited by losing independent IXI validation and training-run disclosures, inconsistent rotation-loss formulas between Section 6.3 and Appendix 15, and an abstract-wide state-of-the-art claim broader than the paper's own lung and supervised-Learn2Reg qualifications.
